newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan dollar down as c.bank counters speculators.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan dollar down as c.bank counters speculators.

text.p: The Taiwan dollar opened lower against the U.S. dollar on Tuesday but was recovering on what dealers said were central bank moves to fend off overseas speculators' efforts to manipulate the local currency.
The Taiwan dollar slumped at the open to T$27.935, below the currency's eight-year closing low, as overseas interests sought to test the central bank's defensive bottom line, dealers said.
True to recent form, the central bank entered to muscle the Taiwan dollar back up, dealers said. After 30 minutes, at 0130 GMT, the unit was at T$27.914 against Monday's T$27.909 close.
Turnover through dealers was an active US$39 million.

Dealers said the Taiwan dollar sank on Monday mainly on foreign fund outflows and strong military demand for the American currency to pay for scheduled arms imports, but that speculative pressure from overseas interests also was seen in the form of non-delivery forward trading.

"We believe there was a lot of NDF buying on the greenback on Monday from foreign funds, which tried to manipulate the Taiwan dollar just like they have done recently in Thailand and the Philippines," said one dealer.
Further overseas speculation was seen early on Tuesday, dealers said.
The dealer said the strategy was unlikely to succeed in Taiwan, where foreign exchange transactions remain subject to strict reporting requirements and central bank limits.

"Taiwan is not Thailand or the Philippines. Taiwan's central bank, which is more powerful, entered to fight speculation both on Monday and this morning and it had easily smoothed the Taiwan dollar depreciation," he said.
The central bank's foreign exchange department declined to take reporters' questions about its reported intervention.
"The bank has a policy of not commenting on such reports," a department official told Reuters.
Another dealer said called the moves by overseas speculators "short-term game-playing" to test the central bank's resolve to stabilise the Taiwan dollar.
"(Speculators) know they can't succeed but are just playing around to test the central bank's bottom line," he said.
A T$27.90-94 range was seen for Tuesday.

Taiwan's currency has been on a slow decline since early 1997, with senior analysts polled by Reuters forecasting that the rate would slip to T$28 to the U.S. dollar in the second half -- but only when the central bank is ready.
